title: SmartPath: hybrid runtime heuristic for kernel allocation balancing prefill priority and tail-latency in mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Reduce 95th/99th-tail latency for mixed workloads (short chat turns + long prefill jobs) while minimizing per-token cost. SmartPath is a hybrid heuristic that combines a compact runtime fingerprint with a lightweight online cost model to pick kernel implementations and prefill/decode scheduling decisions per GPU node and per-request.

Problem context: Our fleet frequently serves mixed traffic where the distribution of sequence lengths changes quickly (e.g., bursts of short chat with occasional long-context completions). Current static kernel routing or global seqlen buckets either overprovision for worst-case (increasing cost) or under-provision for tail latency (causing SLA violations). We need a per-worker, low-overhead tuner that: 1) recognizes transient shifts in seqlen distribution, 2) prefers low-latency kernels for short-decode paths, and 3) safely falls back to throughput-optimized kernels for sustained long-prefill workloads.

Approach summary:
- Runtime fingerprint: stream lightweight metrics per-worker (recent 1k requests): median and 90th/95th seqlen, recent decode token rate, average KV cache hit ratio, and short-job fraction. These are encoded into a 6-d fingerprint vector stored in shared memory (small fixed-size).
- Cost model: approximate per-kernel cost surfaces built from microbenchmarks (tokens/sec, warmup penalty, memory headroom) per architecture class (A100, H100, L4). We compress the empirical tables into a small lookup grid plus linear interpolation to keep evaluation cheap.
- Decision rules: a two-stage policy. First, map fingerprint -> kernel candidate set using thresholded rules (short-high-priority, long-throughput, mixed-hybrid). Second, run a policy comparator that factors in estimated latency impact, rollback risk, and expected unit cost. Includes a fast safety-check that prevents switching if there are >N active long-prefill jobs.
- Prefill/Decode scheduling: when a kernel switch is expected to increase prefill throughput at the cost of decode latency, SmartPath can schedule long-prefill jobs into a separate per-node queue processed during idle intervals or routed to reserved dedicated pools if configured.

Why different from previous work: Many existing tickets focus on global or seqlen-bucketed autotuners. SmartPath favors per-worker transient detection and explicit prefill scheduling with a small safety envelope for rollback. The emphasis is on low memory and compute overhead so the heuristic can live in the hot path of the serving agent without adding tracing or heavy profiling cost.
acceptance_criteria: Proof-of-concept SmartPath enabled on 2 dev clusters (A100 & H100) with runtime flag
Measured 20-40% reduction in 95th latency for a synthetic mixed workload (50k reqs) vs baseline kernel routing
No more than 5% increase in mean cost per token across mixed workload experiments
Safe rollback path implemented (configurable cooldown and active-job threshold)
Unit + integration tests covering fingerprint stability and decision-rule boundaries
Design doc (Confluence) and benchmarking notebooks published and linked from ticket
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Raman: Initial outline completed. Ran offline analysis on production traces (last 30 days) to estimate frequency of mixed-burst patterns. Found ~12% of requests are >1024 tokens but often cluster temporally, motivating per-worker heuristics.

2025-02-18 - Lucas Meyer: Implemented basic fingerprint collector and shared-memory ring buffer. Microbench harness added in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-microbench/tree/eng-59901. Early numbers (A100): two kernels ('short-latency-v1', 'throughput-v2') show 1.8x token/sec difference on long-prefill but 2.1x lower latency on short-decode for the latency kernel.

2025-02-21 - Design review (PM + SRE): Agreed on safety parameters: cooldown default 120s, active-job threshold 4. Action: add metric emission for every kernel decision (prometheus histograms) and a dashboard template.

2025-02-26 - Experiment note: On H100 dev node we observed oscillation when cooldown was 30s. Increasing cooldown to 90s reduced oscillation but hurt adaptability. Decided to implement exponential backoff-style cooldown for frequent flapping patterns.

2025-03-01 - PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2849 (SmartPath: fingerprint collector + policy engine). Requesting reviewers: @maria-ops, @zhang-li. Tests added: fingerprint unit tests + decision boundary fuzzing.

2025-03-03 - Feedback from SRE (Maria Gomez): Add a circuit-breaker to disable SmartPath per-node if memory pressure > 85% or GPU SM occupancy suffers. Also request logging of the reason for every fallback to throughput kernel.

2025-03-05 - Lucas Meyer: Implemented backoff cooldown and circuit-breaker. Preparing canary rollout plan to 5% of production traffic with detailed dashboard and alerting thresholds. Added Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/SmartPath+Hybrid+Heuristic
notes: Planned rollout: enable SmartPath on non-critical tenant groups first (dev/staging) then canary 5% prod -> 20% -> 100%. Monitor 95/99 latency, kernel-switch rate, and cost. If oscillation persists, consider increasing fingerprint window size or switching to Bayesian smoothing of seqlen estimates.

Integrate with Dedicated capacity policy: allow SmartPath to prefer dedicated pools for long-prefill routing
Expand microbench corpus to include quantized kernels and smaller GPUs (L4)
